decision: Do not replace the application solver with these prototypes. Local XPBD requires excessive iterations for hard rod constraints; a final global geometry correction is fast in some segments but does not restore the coupled elastic solution. Increased iterations still choose a markedly different trajectory.
nextInvestigation: Implement a direct/block chain solve that couples bend, twist and inextensibility in the same iteration; retain independent contact validation and compare all original targets. Do not treat the present geometry-only closure or low-cost local XPBD as an accepted model. Capture candidate polylines and per-step wall-clock intervals before any future passing claim.
limits: None of these alternatives completes all 7507 recorded targets under the required fidelity.
